focus: a complete KTZ-style dependency chain ending in one global polynomial and exponent $1-o(1)$

messages.body_markdown: Please target `E2E-15`: for fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, prove a label-aware dichotomy giving either one decoder or a rank-reaching relation with $D\le K_\theta d$. The accepted balanced-color construction shows why a universal cardinality-only reaching family cannot suffice; the direct-decode branch is essential.

The intended argument uses the formal implicit root at a simple point, more than $\Delta$ compatible directions to kill homogeneous terms through degree $\Delta$, and irreducibility to conclude $C\sim Z-Q$. Researcher-0003:P7 is only audit-inexact evidence.

messages.body_markdown: The constant-factor bound in `E2E-21` relies essentially on $D=O_\theta(d)$. If the incidence output only gives $D\le A_\theta d\epsilon^{-\theta/(1-\theta)}$, then the factor list is unbounded and the earlier heavy-factor-or-cross-factor decoder remains necessary.
messages.subject: Do not weaken the bounded-weight interface

nodes.label: Bivariate line-versus-point instance
nodes.notes: The scope is exactly prime field, dimension two, and $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and, after fixing an affine parametrization of every line $L$, a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$. Put $$\rho=d/p,\qquad \epsilon=\operatorname{Agr}_{\mathrm{LVP}}(f,P)=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\mathrm{tot}}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Accepted graph and completion predicate
nodes.notes: Edge mass and point agreement have compatible normalizations.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$G_{\mathrm{acc}}=(\mathbb F_p^2,\mathcal L_p,E_{\mathrm{acc}}),\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\{(x,L):x\in L,\ P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq G_{\mathrm{acc}}$, set $e(G)=|E|/[p^2(p+1)]$. For $c>0$, let $\mathsf{Done}_c$ assert that some total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $Q$ satisfies $\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Fixed-eta reduction
nodes.notes: It suffices to prove the quantitative engine for $0<\theta\le1/4$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Then $0<\theta\le1/4$ and, because $0<\rho<1$, $$\rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component measures
nodes.notes: This begins the exact accepted KTZ component chain.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected accepted graph, let $k$ be its minimum degree, and put $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$|X|/p^2\ge k/(4p),\qquad \tau\ge k/(4p).$$

nodes.label: KTZ reaching family
nodes.notes: This is the accepted cardinality-based selector.
nodes.statement_markdown:
There is $R\subseteq T$ with $$4|T|/k\le|R|\le16|T|/k,
\qquad |R|\ge p+1,$$ such that, for every $L\in T$, more than half of the accepted neighbors of $L$ also lie on an accepted line $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: KTZ weighted interpolant
nodes.notes: The degree $D$ is controlled by the number of selected lines, producing the classical exponent barrier.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $$D=16(\lfloor\sqrt{d|R|}\rfloor+1),$$ there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ with $\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D$, $A_Z\not\equiv0$, and $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$ Moreover $D/k<1/5000$ and $D<k\le p<|R|$.

nodes.label: KTZ reached-root extension
nodes.notes: Each restriction has degree at most $D$ and more than $D$ distinct reached roots.
nodes.statement_markdown: The relation extends to every component line: $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0\qquad(L\in T).$$

nodes.label: KTZ characteristic-safe cleanup
nodes.notes: The resultant bound avoids discriminant and separability errors.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is primitive, squarefree, and of total degree below $p$. Some formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ satisfies $\gcd(B,\mathcal D B)=1$, and an exceptional set obeys $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside it, the line identities for $B$ hold and $\mathcal D B$ is nonzero at accepted points.

nodes.label: KTZ clean minimum-degree core
nodes.notes: The surviving graph need not remain connected.
nodes.statement_markdown: One has $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|/|E|\le D/k+16384dp/k^2<1/4000.$$ Deleting exceptional edges and peeling below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty graph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: KTZ simple accepted roots
nodes.notes: Two distinct retained directions force vertical simplicity.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every point vertex $x$ of $G_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component decoder
nodes.notes: This exact package ends in one polynomial rather than a list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of `E2E-04`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge k/(800p).$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root frontier
nodes.notes: The implication is exactly accepted, but its fixed-$\Lambda$ component antecedent is not supplied by local agreement.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $k_0=\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If a component of the KTZ-pruned core has line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$ for fixed $\Lambda\ge1$, then $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}(d/p)^{1/2}$$ yields one degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $\epsilon/160000$.

nodes.label: Universal reaching-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This forces a decode alternative in any improved selector; it is not a soundness counterexample.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$, there is a legal constant-label table with $$1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$$ such that every family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge Kp/16\ge p/(32\epsilon),$$ although a constant global polynomial already has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching relation interface
nodes.notes: Actual restriction rank replaces the cardinality of a universal selected-line family.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $D\ge d$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\}$$ and define $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\prod_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},
\qquad A\mapsto(A(M(t),P_M(t)))_{M\in R}.$$ For an accepted $G=(X,T,E)$, call $(G,R,D)$ rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D$, and every $L\in T$ has more than $D$ accepted neighbors lying also on an accepted line in $R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal incidence bottleneck. `E2E-13` explains why its decoder branch cannot be omitted.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta>0$ and $0<a_\theta\le1$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ either $\mathsf{Done}_{a_\theta}$ holds, or there are an accepted graph $G=(X,T,E)$, a set $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ satisfying $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d,$$ for which $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter gate
nodes.notes: If the trigger exceeds $1$, there is no instance and the implication is vacuous.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation branch, $$D/(\epsilon p)\le K_\theta\rho/\epsilon\le(K_\theta/C_\theta)\rho^\theta\le K_\theta/C_\theta.$$ Enlarging $C_\theta$ therefore ensures $$D\le a_\theta\epsilon p/10^4<p.$$ This uses no assumption such as $p\ge d^C$.

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: No P3 evidence is attached: the accepted P3 proves a cardinality-based construction, not this rank-kernel statement.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the relation branch there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\\quad(M\in R),
\qquad A_Z\not\equiv0.$$ Indeed, a kernel element exists by rank deficiency; taking its product of distinct irreducible factors preserves every line identity; $|R|>D$ excludes a $Z$-independent relation; and $D<p$ then implies $A_Z\not\equiv0$.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching root extension
nodes.notes: `E2E-07` is the exact accepted root-count template; the strengthened input still needs its own formal statement.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, the more than $D$ reached accepted points are roots of the degree-at-most-$D$ restriction, so $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Abstract whole-relation cleanup
nodes.notes: `E2E-08` supplies the accepted template. Evidence is intentionally not transferred to this strengthened interface before an exact audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$ using the coefficient content $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$. Then $B$ is primitive in $Z$, squarefree, and of total degree below $p$. There are a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal D B)=1$ and an exceptional edge set such that $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside this set, all retained line identities for $B$ hold and $\mathcal D B$ is nonzero at accepted points.

nodes.label: Global clean simple-root core
nodes.notes: This uses a global vertex-count peeling bound instead of the component-local condition $k^2\gtrsim dp$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
The exceptional normalized mass satisfies $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|/[p^2(p+1)]\le(D/p)^2+D/p.$$ Delete these edges and iteratively delete vertices of current degree at most $D$. After increasing $C_\theta$ if necessary, the remaining graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ satisfies, for $b_\theta=a_\theta/2$, $$e(G_1)\ge b_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(G_1)>D.$$ Every retained line has the $B$-identity, and every retained point satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Bounded factor partition and heavy class
nodes.notes: The bound $D\le K_\theta d$ eliminates the earlier heavy-factor-or-cross-factor-decoder obligation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducibles and set $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}C_i$. Primitivity implies that every $C_i$ depends on $Z$, hence $$s\le\deg_ZB\le D/d\le K_\theta.$$ Vertical simplicity partitions $G_1$ uniquely into factor classes $G_{1,i}$, preserving minimum degree, with $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\quad C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\quad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0.$$ Some class has mass $\mu_i=e(G_{1,i})\ge b_\theta\epsilon/K_\theta$, and each of its point vertices has more than $D\ge\Delta_i$ factor-consistent incident lines.

nodes.label: High-direction factor linearization
nodes.notes: The cited source is audit-inexact and rejected as a whole, so this node still needs a fresh exact proof.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C=C_i$ and $\Delta=\Delta_i<D<p$. At a point where $C_Z\ne0$, more than $\Delta$ compatible degree-at-most-$d$ graph directions determine a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0.$$ Since $C$ is irreducible and depends on $Z$, it follows that $$C\sim Z-Q.$$

nodes.label: All heavy-factor edges charge to one polynomial
nodes.notes: This is the list-to-single conversion; it uses neither connectivity nor a Vinh estimate.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every point vertex $x$ of the heavy factor class, $C_i(x,f(x))=0$ and $C_i\sim Z-Q$ imply $Q(x)=f(x)$. Since $$|E_{1,i}|\le(p+1)|X_{1,i}|,$$ one has $$|X_{1,i}|/p^2\ge e(G_{1,i})\ge b_\theta\epsilon/K_\theta.$$ Combining this with the direct branch of `E2E-15` proves $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$ for $c_\theta=\min\{a_\theta,b_\theta/K_\theta\}$.

nodes.label: Close every fixed exponent
nodes.notes: The constants depend only on the fixed parameter $\eta$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For fixed $\eta>0$, apply the chain with $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. The implication $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\theta}$$ yields one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial with agreement at least $c_\eta\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Uniform exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: This stronger statement is refuted at the legal degree $d=101$; its enclosing source audit is `revise`. The fixed-$\eta$ goal remains compatible with the counterexample.
nodes.statement_markdown: There exist absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that every legal instance satisfying $\epsilon\ge C d/p$ also satisfies $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate soundness
nodes.notes: Blocked on `E2E-15` and exact formalization of `E2E-17` through `E2E-22`, especially factor linearization. Work states report activity, not proof status.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every legal bivariate line table, $$\operatorname{Agr}_{\mathrm{LVP}}(f,P)\ge C_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\operatorname{Agr}_{\mathrm{LVP}}(f,P).$$

summary: Round 1 records the complete exact accepted KTZ component chain in `E2E-04` through `E2E-11`; its available fixed-component refinement reaches only the conditional square-root frontier `E2E-12`. The near-linear route replaces cardinality interpolation with the open bounded-weight rank-or-decode interface `E2E-15`. Its relation branch gives a squarefree global relation, reached-root extension, characteristic-safe cleanup, a positive-mass simple-root core, and only $O_\theta(1)$ factor classes. A heavy factor can then be linearized as $Z-Q$, allowing all of its edges across all components to charge directly to one global polynomial without Vinh mixing. The goal remains blocked on the new incidence dichotomy and exact audits of the strengthened algebraic transfers; the uniform exact exponent-one endpoint is separately refuted.
target_statement: Prove that soundness at least $(d/p)^{1-o(1)}$ yields agreement with one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial for $100<d<p$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
title: End-to-end soundness chain
